messages:
sarah: Heads up — this morning we hit a weird double-provisioning loop when the eu-west1 GPU pool ran out and requests spilled to the us-central cluster. Observed: CA created nodes in both regions, pods kept bouncing until nodeAffinity kicked in.
mateo: Ugh. Do you have the pod log + CA events? was it spot -> ondemand fallback?
ops-bot: [autoscaler] 2026-03-17T08:23:12Z scale: group=gpu-eu-west1 size: 0->4 reason=unschedulable pods=12 backlog=1
ops-bot: [autoscaler] 2026-03-17T08:23:16Z scale: group=gpu-us-central size: 2->6 reason=fallback-from-region capacity-check-failed in eu-west1
yun: From the events I pulled, CA saw pods unschedulable, attempted eu-west1 first, then triggered the expander fallback which considers both price and capacity. Because our podSpec lacks strict nodeAffinity and only tolerates the gpu taint, the scheduler allowed cross-region bind while image pull secrets + network egress rules caused long init times -> more reschedules.
ivan: I think the root cause is threefold: (1) no preferredDuringScheduling nodeAffinity to prefer same-region nodes, (2) CA max-node-provision-time is too low so it kept trying other groups, (3) we have mixed GPU SKUs which made the scheduler treat nodes as compatible when they're not (nv4 vs a100).
sarah: Agree. Short-term mitigation idea: add a soft nodeAffinity to prefer region-local nodes and tighten the expander to "most-pods" or set weights so eu pools beat others. Also increase `--max-node-provision-time` to 10m so CA waits for the first group.
mateo: Can we do a config like this?
mateo: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-job
spec:
  tolerations:
    - key: "gpu"
      operator: "Exists"
      effect: "NoSchedule"
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        - weight: 90
          preference:
            matchExpressions:
              - key: topology.kubernetes.io/region
                operator: In
                values: ["eu-west1"]
  containers:
    - name: worker
      image: gcr.io/redwood/worker:latest
      resources:
        limits:
          nvidia.com/gpu: 1
```
yun: That looks right for soft preference. Also add a `priorityClassName` for GPU jobs and a PDB to avoid mass disruption during node churn.
ivan: Longer term: we should encode region affinity at the job template level in the batch controller and make the CA expander use `priority` weights per group. Also add a validation that mixed-GPU SKUs are only schedule-compatible if local runtime shows proper compute capability.
sarah: Cost note — we saw a ~$1.5k spike due to spinning on-image-pull retries and cross-region egress. If we rely on cross-region fallback frequently we should make it opt-in per tenant.
mateo: For the immediate patch I can tweak CA flags: `--max-node-provision-time=600s` and set expander policy to `least-waste` with custom weights for eu pools. I'll also push the nodeAffinity change to the template.
ops-bot: action created: #INC-4321 Create region-pref affinity + CA config tweak (assignee: mateo)
yun: One more: consider a warm pool / reserved standby nodes in each region (small commit) to absorb short surges — much cheaper than cross-region retries and makes latency predictable.
ivan: +1. We'll need to tweak autoscaler scaling policies to avoid resizing warm pools during normal operations. Also add a health probe for GPU driver readiness to reduce init failures causing CA to think provisioning failed.
sarah: Plan summarized: 1) mateo updates batch templates with preferredDuringScheduling affinity + PDB, 2) ops increases `--max-node-provision-time` and adjusts expander weights, 3) infra to prototype 2-4 reserved GPUs per region (warm pool), 4) add GPU driver readiness probe in node bootstrap. I'll run the postmortem tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
mateo: I'll start the CA flag PR and a quick canary in staging today.
ivan: I'll draft the playbook for on-call to avoid flipping regions blindly.
ops-bot: [deploy] canary: CA-config-pr -> staging (requires manual approval)
sarah: Thanks team — looping in @oncall for visibility. If anyone sees a similar cross-region churn, ping this thread.
